## Water-Quality Data Coverage

<!--
Outline: data coverage checks
- Use @tbl-data-summary and @fig-monitoring-coverage. The raw count is 25,665 observations across 174 unique site identifiers. Chlorophyll-a has 1,847 raw records, so correct the narrative value of 1,845.
- Processing retains 11,946 observations (46.5%) in 291 parameter-specific bin records. There are 286 finite bin means: chlorophyll-a 25 of 27, dissolved oxygen 68 of 68, salinity 67 of 67, turbidity 58 of 61, and temperature 68 of 68. Do not describe all 291 records as usable predictor values.
- Keep the chlorophyll-a exclusion and the main spatial coverage gaps. Correct the incomplete phrase "using 666" to identify observations and the typo "fo" in the existing paragraph.
-->

There were 25,665 raw observations from across all five parameter datasets, representing 174 unique site locations. Chlorophyll-a had 1,845 records from 54 sites. Processing resulted in 27 binned values using 666. Dissolved Oxygen had 6,261 observations from 169 sites. Processing reduced the data to 68 binned values using 3,010 observations. Salinity returned 6,994 observation values from 159 sites. The data was processed into 67 binned values using 3,400 observations.  Turbidity had 3,402 observed values from 146 sites. After processing there were 61 binned values using 1,429 observations. Water temperature had 7,161 raw observations from 169 sites. Data processing returned 68 binned values using 3,441 observations. Overall, data processing returned 291 parameterized data values using 11,946 fo the 25,665 original values, representing 46.5% of the original dataset (@tbl-data-summary).

For all parameters, the data was heavily skewed spatially, with the majority of samples located in Escambia and Pensacola Bays. Chlorophyll-a in particular had much fewer sites and almost no observations located in the eastern half of the study area. Due to such a lack of spatial distribution, chlorophyll-a was subsequently dropped from the analysis (@fig-monitoring-coverage). 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of raw and processed warm-season water-quality data by environmental parameter."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

wq_summary <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Parameter,      ~`Raw observations`, ~`Raw stations`, ~`Retained observations`, ~`Retained stations`, ~`Spatial bins`,
  "Chlorophyll-a", 1847,                54,              666,                      48,                   27,
  "Dissolved Oxygen",            6261,                169,             3010,                     145,                  68,
  "Salinity",      6994,                159,             3400,                     135,                  67,
  "Turbidity",     3402,                146,             1429,                     122,                  61,
  "Temperature",   7161,                169,             3441,                     145,                  68
)

knitr::kable(
  wq_summary,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
  digits = 0,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-monitoring-coverage
#| fig-cap: "Spatial distribution of monitoring stations represented in each raw water-quality dataset."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

monitoring_sites <- imap_dfr(
  raw_data,
  \(data, parameter) {
    data %>%
      dplyr::select(Location_Identifier, geometry) %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(Location_Identifier)) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(Location_Identifier) %>%
      dplyr::slice(1) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(parameter = parameter)
  }
) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  st_transform(st_crs(study_area))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = study_area,
    fill = "grey95",
    color = "grey45",
    linewidth = 0.25
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = monitoring_sites,
    color = "#2166AC",
    size = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.65
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

## Environmental Predictor Results

<!--
Outline: shared environmental results
- Use @fig-ipdw-sensitivity for sensitivity, @tbl-ipdw-validation for repeated validation at the chosen settings, @tbl-raster-summary for raster ranges, and @fig-environmental-rasters for spatial patterns. There is no fig-processed-mean-distributions chunk in this document.
- All four selected water-quality surfaces use power 0.25 and range 10 km. Describe the values with SDs as repeated validation summaries, rather than statistics from the separate seed-42 final check.
- Add oyster recruitment: 10 input sites, values 0 to 14.76; saved validation MAE 5.510, RMSE 6.481, bias -0.808, and 100% coverage. Its raster has 33,323 finite cells, mean 7.354 and SD 3.035. Supply units and the validation-fold setup before finalizing this paragraph. The current shared tables and map omit recruitment.
-->

Each parameter (save for chlorophyll-a) was interpolated into predicted surface rasters using an inverse-path distance weighting algorithm. To ensure the highest accuracy was achieved, a sensitivy analysis was conducted on each parameter model using 36 distance-power/range combinations, which were in turn evaluated across five random five-fold spatial partitions. Powers ranged from 0.25 to 3.00, and  maximum range values evaluated were 5, 10, 15, and 20 km (@fig-ipdw-sensitivity). 

While the results of every sensitivity analysis will be reported here, it should be noted that after running all parameters it was decided that a distance power of 0.25 and a max range of 10km was to be used. This decision was made as there was little variation in results of the sensitivity analysis and a smoother prediction surface was preferred to better represent the smoother gradients found in the real world. 

```{r}
#| label: fig-ipdw-sensitivity
#| fig-cap: "Mean MAE across distance-power and maximum-range combinations evaluated using repeated five-fold spatial cross-validation. Red outlines identify the parameter combinations used for the final interpolation models."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

plot_sensitivity <- function(result, stats, parameter) {
  power_levels <- sort(unique(result$summary$dist_power))
  range_levels <- sort(unique(result$summary$max_range))

  plot_data <- result$summary %>%
    mutate(
      dist_power = factor(dist_power, levels = power_levels),
      max_range = factor(max_range, levels = range_levels)
    )

  selected_data <- result$summary %>%
    filter(
      near(dist_power, stats$dist_power[[1]]),
      max_range == stats$max_range[[1]]
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      dist_power = factor(dist_power, levels = power_levels),
      max_range = factor(max_range, levels = range_levels)
    )

  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = dist_power,
      y = max_range,
      fill = mean_MAE
    )
  ) +
    geom_tile() +
    geom_tile(
      data = selected_data,
      fill = NA,
      color = "red",
      linewidth = 1.2
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(
        label = sprintf("%.2f", mean_MAE),
        color = mean_MAE > median(mean_MAE, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      size = 3
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      direction = -1,
      name = "Mean MAE"
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("FALSE" = "black", "TRUE" = "white"),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = parameter,
      x = "Distance power",
      y = "Maximum range (m)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    )
}

sensitivity_plots <- imap(
  sensitivity_results,
  \(result, parameter) {
    plot_sensitivity(
      result = result,
      stats = model_stats[[parameter]],
      parameter = parameter
    )
  }
)

wrap_plots(sensitivity_plots, ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "IPDW Parameter Sensitivity Analysis",
    subtitle = "Repeated five-fold spatial cross-validation"
  )
```

### Dissolved Oxygen

<!--
Outline: dissolved oxygen check
- Round the lowest sensitivity MAE consistently to 0.426 mg/L (power 0.75, range 10 km). Selected-setting MAE is 0.431 (SD 0.006), RMSE 0.552 (SD 0.004), bias +0.013, coverage 100% (@tbl-ipdw-validation).
- Correct "rater" and check the geographic wording against @fig-environmental-rasters; the current sentence describes a westward decrease but places the lowest values in East Bay and northern Blackwater Bay.
-->

Dissolved oxygen sensitivity had a mean MAE ranging from 0.426 to 0.507 mg/L. The lowest mean MAE with 100% prediction was 0.425mg/L using a distance power of 0.75 and max range of 10km (@tbl-ipdw-validation). The predicted rater surface values ranged from 5.28mg/L to 7.99mg/L (n = 33,792; µ = 6.52; σ = 0.26; @tbl-raster-summary). The final prediction model achieved 100% coverage with a MAE of 0.431 mg/L (σ = 0.006) with RMSE = 0.552 mg/L (σ = 0.004). The model tended to over predict by +0.013 mg/L. Spatially, dissolved oxygen generally decreased in the western portions of the study area. With the lowest values appearing in East Bay and northern Blackwater Bay (@fig-environmental-rasters).   


### Salinity

<!--
Outline: salinity check
- Clarify the MAE comparison: selected 0.25/10 km = 2.490102 ppt; best with full coverage, 0.50/10 km = 2.489983 ppt; difference = 0.000119 ppt. The overall minimum, 3.00/5 km = 2.397423 ppt, differs from the selected result by 0.092679 ppt and has mean coverage 96.1% (@fig-ipdw-sensitivity).
-->

The salinity sensitivity analysis had a mean MAE ranging from 2.397 ppt to 3.125 ppt. The lowest reported MAE with 100% model coverage was 2.49 ppt using distance power 0.50 and max range of 10km. The absolute lowest mean MAE was 2.397 ppt was achieved using distance power of 3.00 and a max range of 5km , but model coverage fell to 96.1%. The difference in mean MAE between the lowest achieved DP-MR combination and the actual DP-MR combination used was 0.000119 ppt (@tbl-ipdw-validation). Spatial cross-validation of the final model fit had a MAE of 2.49 ppt (σ = 0.036) and RMSE 3.444 ppt (σ = 0.024). The model slightly over predicted salinity values (+0.140 ppt) and achieved 100% coverage. The predicted values ranged from 2.31 to 26.73 ppt (n = 33,792; µ = 16.36 ppt; σ = 3.14; @tbl-raster-summary). Spatially, salinity generally decreased from west to east with the lowest values being in the northern Blackwater Bay and the highest values located in the southwestern region of Pensacola Bay (@fig-environmental-rasters). 

### Turbidity

<!--
Outline: turbidity coverage
- Explain that 95.1% is 58 valid observed/predicted pairs out of 61 bin records. Three bins have nonfinite observed means after outlier exclusion; this percentage alone does not show failed interpolation (@tbl-ipdw-validation).
-->

The sensitivity analysis for turbidity reported a mean MAE range from 0.696 to 0.847 NTU. The lowest mean MAE was 0.696 NTU (DP = 1.00, MR = 15km) with 95.1% model coverage (@tbl-ipdw-validation). The final model fit produced a MAE = 0.745 NTU (σ = 0.018) with RMSE = 0.937 NTU (σ = 0.026). Overall the model slightly under predicted by -0.010 NTU and achieved 95.1% coverage. The final predicted surface values ranged from 0.03 NTU to 5.23 NTU (n = 33,790; µ = 2.23 NTU; σ = 0.47; @tbl-raster-summary). Spatially, turbidity generally decreased from north to south, with the highest values occuring near the mouth of Escambia River and the lowest values occuring in the southwestern portion of Pensacola Bay (@fig-environmental-rasters).

### Water Temperature

<!--
Outline: temperature and raster summaries
- The existing temperature values match the saved repeated summaries. Keep the shared raster ranges: dissolved oxygen 5.28 to 7.99 mg/L, salinity 2.31 to 26.73 ppt, turbidity 0.03 to 5.23 NTU, and temperature 25.93 to 30.43 degrees C (@tbl-raster-summary). Raster counts are 33,792 for each except turbidity, which has 33,790.
-->

Mean MAE for the water temperature sensitivity analysis ranged from 0.978 to 1.135 degrees C. The lowest mean MAE was 0.978 degrees C with 100% model coverage (DP = 0.75, MR = 10km; @tbl-ipdw-validation). The final model had a MAE of 0.988 degrees C (σ = 0.015) and RMSE was 1.163 degrees C (σ = 0.014). The model generally under predicted water temperature by -0.063 degrees C with 100% model coverage. The resulting prediction surface ranged from 25.93 to 30.43 degrees C (n = 33,792; µ = 27.66°C; σ = 0.41°C; @tbl-raster-summary). Water temperature was generally lower in the eastern portions of the study area, with the coolest values trending toward Blackwater Bay (@fig-environmental-rasters). 



```{r}
#| label: tbl-ipdw-validation
#| tbl-cap: "Selected IPDW parameters and repeated spatial cross-validation performance. Values in parentheses are standard deviations across random spatial partitions."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

validation_summary <- imap_dfr(
  model_stats,
  \(stats, parameter) {
    selected_power <- stats$dist_power[[1]]
    selected_range <- stats$max_range[[1]]

    repeated_results <- sensitivity_results[[parameter]]$summary %>%
      filter(
        near(dist_power, selected_power),
        max_range == selected_range
      ) %>%
      slice(1)

    tibble(
      Parameter = parameter,
      Units = parameter_units[[parameter]],
      `Distance power` = selected_power,
      `Maximum range (km)` = selected_range / 1000,
      `Mean MAE (SD)` = sprintf(
        "%.3f (%.3f)",
        repeated_results$mean_MAE,
        repeated_results$sd_MAE
      ),
      `Mean RMSE (SD)` = sprintf(
        "%.3f (%.3f)",
        repeated_results$mean_RMSE,
        repeated_results$sd_RMSE
      ),
      `Mean bias` = sprintf(
        "%.3f",
        repeated_results$mean_Bias
      ),
      `Mean coverage` = scales::percent(
        repeated_results$mean_coverage,
        accuracy = 0.1
      )
    )
  }
)

kable(
  validation_summary,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-raster-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of final IPDW environmental predictor rasters."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

raster_summary <- imap_dfr(
  raster_results,
  \(raster_layer, parameter) {
    raster_values <- getValues(raster_layer)
    raster_resolution <- res(raster_layer)

    tibble(
      Parameter = parameter,
      Units = parameter_units[[parameter]],
      Minimum = min(raster_values, na.rm = TRUE),
      Maximum = max(raster_values, na.rm = TRUE),
      `Predicted cells` = sum(!is.na(raster_values)),
      `Cell size` = paste0(
        raster_resolution[[1]],
        " x ",
        raster_resolution[[2]],
        " m"
      )
    )
  }
) %>%
  mutate(
    Minimum = sprintf("%.2f", Minimum),
    Maximum = sprintf("%.2f", Maximum),
    `Predicted cells` = scales::comma(`Predicted cells`)
  )

kable(
  raster_summary,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "c")
)
```

## MaxEnt Model Tuning and Selection

<!--
Outline: current tuning and performance results
- Report 24 candidates across four spatial partitions. Selected configuration: LQH, regularization multiplier 0.5, and 14 nonzero coefficients. Selection uses lowest mean 10th-percentile omission, then highest mean Continuous Boyce Index.
- Selected mean validation AUC = 0.703 (SD 0.136); omission = 11.46% (SD 9.10 percentage points); Continuous Boyce Index = 0.093 (SD 0.525). Training AUC = 0.862. These summarize the tuning folds, rather than independent validation.
- Fold AUC/omission: 1 = 0.843/11.1%, 2 = 0.582/0%, 3 = 0.590/22.2%, 4 = 0.796/12.5%. Held-out presence counts are 9, 8, 9, and 8; background counts are 5,706, 432, 2,594, and 1,268. Briefly mention the variation among partitions.
- Selected AICc = 691.295 and delta AICc = 13.590. The minimum-AICc candidate is LQ/0.5 (AICc 677.705; validation AUC 0.520; omission 22.22%). Do not describe the selected model as the minimum-AICc model.
- Use maxent_tuning_results.csv, maxent_selected_settings.csv, and maxent_cross_validation_metrics.csv in 4-tables-and-figures/tables. Adapt @tbl-maxent-selection to these saved columns before citing it; its current RDS input does not exist.
-->



```{r}
#| label: tbl-maxent-selection
#| tbl-cap: "Performance of the leading candidate MaxEnt configurations."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

maxent_tuning <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "models", "maxent_tuning_results.rds")
)

maxent_tuning_table <- maxent_tuning %>%
  arrange(desc(selected), delta_aicc) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  transmute(
    `Feature class` = feature_class,
    `Regularization multiplier` = regularization_multiplier,
    `Mean AUC` = sprintf("%.3f", mean_auc),
    `Mean omission rate` = sprintf("%.3f", mean_omission_rate),
    `Mean Boyce index` = sprintf("%.3f", mean_boyce),
    `Delta AICc` = sprintf("%.2f", delta_aicc),
    Selected = if_else(selected, "Yes", "No")
  )

kable(
  maxent_tuning_table,
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-variable-importance

variable_importance <- readRDS(

)

importance_long <- variable_importance %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(contribution, permutation_importance),
    names_to = "metric",

  ) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = recode(
      metric,
      contribution = "Contribution",

    ),
    variable = fct_reorder(variable, importance, .fun = max)
  )

ggplot(

    y = variable,
    fill = metric
  )
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2166AC", "#B2182B")) +
  labs(
    x = "Importance (%)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

## Comparison with the Existing HSI

<!--
Outline: HSI comparison results and remaining description
- Current inputs are 2-data/hsm/normalized_suitability.tif and 2-data/rasters/maxent_suitability.tif. Reproducing the existing comparison steps on November 19 gives 31,774 paired 100 m cells (317.74 square km), less than the full MaxEnt prediction area.
- Exact agreement across the five equal-interval classes = 27.54%; agreement within one class = 73.38%; continuous Spearman rho = 0.273. Report the paired area, class boundaries, and these values in @tbl-hsi-comparison after updating its inputs and metrics.
- Use @fig-hsi-comparison for the main agreement/disagreement locations. Available maps are 4-tables-and-figures/maps/hsi_suitability.png, maxent_suitability.png, and model_favorability.png. Add a geographic description after inspecting the final maps.
- The comparison notebook maps HSI class minus MaxEnt class, while the report placeholder maps continuous MaxEnt minus HSI. Choose the intended difference and match the caption and sign interpretation. @fig-hsi-scatter is optional and still disabled.
-->



```{r}
#| label: tbl-hsi-comparison
#| tbl-cap: "Cell-level comparison between MaxEnt and HSI habitat-suitability predictions."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

maxent_suitability <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "models", "maxent_suitability.rds")
)

hsi_suitability <- readRDS(
  here("2-data", "models", "hsi_suitability.rds")
)

compareRaster(
  maxent_suitability,
  hsi_suitability,
  extent = TRUE,
  rowcol = TRUE,
  crs = TRUE,
  res = TRUE,
  orig = TRUE,
  stopiffalse = TRUE
)

comparison_data <- tibble(
  maxent = getValues(maxent_suitability),
  hsi = getValues(hsi_suitability)
) %>%
  drop_na()

hsi_comparison <- tibble(
  Metric = c(
    "Pearson correlation",
    "Spearman correlation",
    "Mean signed difference",
    "Mean absolute difference",
    "Root mean square difference",
    "Cells within 0.10 suitability units"
  ),
  Value = c(
    sprintf("%.3f", cor(comparison_data$maxent, comparison_data$hsi)),
    sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      cor(
        comparison_data$maxent,
        comparison_data$hsi,
        method = "spearman"
      )
    ),
    sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      mean(comparison_data$maxent - comparison_data$hsi)
    ),
    sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      mean(abs(comparison_data$maxent - comparison_data$hsi))
    ),
    sprintf(
      "%.3f",
      sqrt(mean((comparison_data$maxent - comparison_data$hsi)^2))
    ),
    scales::percent(
      mean(abs(comparison_data$maxent - comparison_data$hsi) <= 0.10),
      accuracy = 0.1
    )
  )
)

kable(
  hsi_comparison,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  align = c("l", "r")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-hsi-comparison
#| fig-cap: "Spatial comparison of MaxEnt and HSI habitat-suitability predictions. Positive differences indicate greater suitability predicted by MaxEnt."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

suitability_difference <- maxent_suitability - hsi_suitability

difference_limit <- max(
  abs(range(getValues(suitability_difference), na.rm = TRUE))
)

old_par <- par(
  mfrow = c(1, 3),
  mar = c(2, 2, 3, 5)
)

raster::plot(
  maxent_suitability,
  col = hcl.colors(100, "YlGn"),
  zlim = c(0, 1),
  main = "MaxEnt",
  axes = FALSE,
  box = FALSE
)

raster::plot(
  hsi_suitability,
  col = hcl.colors(100, "YlGn"),
  zlim = c(0, 1),
  main = "HSI",
  axes = FALSE,
  box = FALSE
)

raster::plot(
  suitability_difference,
  col = hcl.colors(100, "Blue-Red 3"),
  zlim = c(-difference_limit, difference_limit),
  main = "MaxEnt minus HSI",
  axes = FALSE,
  box = FALSE
)

par(old_par)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-hsi-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Cell-level relationship between MaxEnt and HSI habitat-suitability predictions. The dashed line represents perfect agreement."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| eval: false

set.seed(42)

comparison_plot_data <- comparison_data %>%
  slice_sample(n = min(20000, n()))

ggplot(
  comparison_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = hsi,
    y = maxent
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    color = "#2166AC",
    alpha = 0.15,
    size = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey30"
  ) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "HSI suitability",
    y = "MaxEnt suitability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
